entry.title: Theory of two-dimensional Wigner crystals with defects: Interactions, melting transitions and collective modes
entry.summary: The physics of Wigner solids is characterized by an interplay of elasticity and long-range electrostatics, endowing crystal defects with properties distinct from those in charge-neutral crystals. Recent experiments observing lattice melting and Wigner-crystal-adjacent phases in two dimensions necessitate an examination of how defects affect the long-wavelength properties of such solids. Here, we use duality techniques to construct a comprehensive framework for studying the contribution of vacancies and interstitials, dislocations, and disclinations to the effective action of two-dimensional charged crystals. This allows for a systematic investigation of the interaction energies for the different combinations of defect pairs. We further study melting transitions due to defect proliferation, assessing and justifying some of the assumptions present in the literature. In the metallic Wigner crystal phase, characterized by a finite ground state density of vacancies, we find phonons with a dispersion relation that varies in an unusual way with the vacancy density. Consequently, we discuss how thermodynamic properties of such a vacancy Fermi liquid can be probed in measurements of the melting temperature and speed of sound. The field theory developed here can serve as a starting point in the study of anomalous Hall crystals and charge density waves with defects.

entry.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
entry.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8σ$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5σ$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

entry.title: Gravitational lensing effects on neutrino oscillations around a Schwarzschild black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
entry.summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the weak gravitational-lensing regime of a static, spherically symmetric black hole surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). Within a covariant quantum-mechanical framework, we derive the oscillation phases for radial and non-radial propagation of ultrarelativistic neutrinos. While the leading radial phase is independent of the metric function, non-radial trajectories acquire impact-parameter-dependent corrections governed by the PFDM parameter $λ$. We construct the flavor-transition probability for two coherent lensed paths and analyze the resulting interference in two and three flavor scenarios. Varying $λ$ shifts the oscillation extrema and modifies their amplitudes and contrast, with a non-monotonic dependence on the neutrino mass scale, lens mass, flavor channel, and mass ordering. The $P_{μτ}$ channel shows particularly strong sensitivity to the PFDM contribution for the considered configurations. Moreover, the path-interference terms retain information about the absolute neutrino mass scale. These results characterize PFDM-induced modifications of lensed neutrino oscillations and provide a basis for more realistic treatments including decoherence, averaging, detector resolution, and corrections to lens trajectories and magnifications.

entry.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
entry.summary: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.

entry.title: Tidal Heating of Stellar Clusters in Fuzzy Dark Matter Halos
entry.summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies serve as powerful testing grounds for wave dark matter models through dynamical stellar heating. Previous simulation-based work derived a lower bound on the fuzzy dark matter particle mass using a diffusion approximation valid only when the de Broglie wavelength is much smaller than the galaxy's half-light radius. We simulate the dynamical evolution of stellar clusters in FDM halos across a wide mass range and find that for sufficiently low masses, where the de Broglie wavelength is much larger than the cluster size, tidal heating is the main mechanism. We also find that a reduced soliton mass and tidally stripped halo can suppress the heating. We demonstrate that in order to constrain FDM mass from cluster heating, the structure and environment of the FDM halo must be carefully considered.

entry.title: Critical limits of accelerating Kerr--NUT spacetimes and the non-expanding Plebański--Demiański family
entry.summary: We study degenerate-horizon limits of vacuum accelerating Kerr--NUT spacetimes with finite, nonzero NUT parameter. At cubic criticality, $a^2=m^2+\ell^2$ and $αm=1$, a projective coordinate transformation relates the complete critical parent metrics by a local homothety. The cubic horizon has one finite axis and a noncompact angular end, and its near-horizon limit is locally homothetic to the swirling universe. Explicit four-dimensional coordinate transformations place the ordinary extremal, Nariai and cubic near-horizon metrics in the negative-, positive- and zero-curvature longitudinal sectors of the non-expanding Plebański--Demiański family. The Nariai correspondence includes an exceptional endpoint that requires a separate Killing chart. Under a cubic-adapted near-critical scaling, fixed first-order separations between the approaching horizons do not affect the leading metric. The global Killing identifications and regular completion of the critical parent remain open.

entry.title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas to Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
entry.summary: We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubic scaling $O(βN^3)$ to linear scaling $O(βN N_e^2)$ with respect to the system size $N$, where $N_e$ is the particle number. This yields a dramatic speedup in dilute regimes ($N_e \ll N$), opening unbiased access to large-scale simulations of strongly correlated low-density phases. We validate the method on the dilute Fermi gas with onsite Hubbard interactions, observing the suppression of the fermion sign problem in the dilute limit. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a one-dimensional flat-band system, where the canonical ensemble allows for precise control over filling. We reveal a ferromagnetic instability at low temperatures in the half-filling regime. Our linear-scaling approach provides a powerful tool for investigating emergent phenomena in dilute quantum matter.

entry.title: Bayesian Inference of Primary Hair from Black Hole Shadows in Generalized Proca Theory
entry.summary: We investigate black hole shadows and observational constraints on primary vector hair in an exact rotating solution of generalized Proca theory. Selecting a coupling slice yields a simple, one-parameter Kerr deformation that is noncircular and depends on spin and latitude. The deformation vanishes in the nonrotating limit, while the vector field remains nontrivial. We determine the domain admitting a regular outer horizon and construct shadow and lensing images by numerical ray tracing. Ray-traced images show a modest enlargement of the shadow and changes in the surrounding lensing pattern. Bayesian inference using the shadow area-equivalent radius and axis ratio yields joint constraints on hair, spin, and viewing inclination from Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87* and Sgr A*. The M87* posterior favors relatively low spin and exhibits a pronounced spin--hair anticorrelation, while Sgr A* yields upper limits on spin and hair with its inclination remaining essentially unconstrained. These results connect the optical signatures of primary vector hair to quantitative horizon-scale constraints.

entry.title: Random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains revisited
entry.summary: We revisit the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-$3/2$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using the tensor-network strong-disorder renormalization group (tSDRG). The predicted transition separates two random-singlet (RS) phases: one formed by effective spin-$1/2$ moments at weaker disorder and the other by full spin-$3/2$ moments at stronger disorder. Within the Damle--Huse classification, this transition corresponds to an emergent permutation-symmetric $\mathcal{P}_4$ multicritical point on a $\mathcal{P}_2$ critical line associated with the RS phases. We first derive the critical exponents governing the disorder-averaged bulk and end-to-end correlation functions in the $\mathcal{P}_n$ universality classes within the Damle--Huse framework. Using these theoretical predictions, together with a diagnostic constructed from the mean and variance of the energy-gap distribution, we identify the $\mathcal{P}_4$ transition point and the reentrant behavior of the RS phase.

entry.title: Complex spinodals and supercritical crossovers in Kerr-Newman-AdS$_4$ black holes
entry.summary: We study supercritical crossovers in four-dimensional Kerr-Newman-AdS black holes at fixed angular momentum and charge. From the exact enthalpy, we prove uniqueness of the physical critical point and positivity of the quartic Landau coefficient throughout the charge-rotation family, treating the uncharged Kerr-AdS endpoint in separate scaling variables. An exact quartic reduction determines the coexistence entropies and latent heat throughout the subcritical regime. Above criticality, the two physical spinodals continue as a complex conjugate pair. Their real temperature projection defines a Widom-type line, and varying the charge-rotation ratio assembles these lines into a crossover surface. The Landau cusp fixes the imaginary entropy and temperature to scale with the square root and three-halves powers of the pressure displacement from criticality. The projected fold and the local heat capacity ridge share a critical tangent. We derive their leading quadratic temperature separation and prove that the ridge lies at a higher temperature near criticality. Exact endpoint solutions and numerical continuation check these predictions. The cusp exponents are common to the family, while the crossover temperature depends on the thermodynamic criterion used to define it.

entry.title: Multi-Band Constraints on Cosmic Strings: Unifying Harmonic and Burst Spectra
entry.summary: Cosmic-string loops generate a broadband gravitational-wave background (GWB) that is typically modeled via two distinct formalisms: a discrete harmonic expansion, commonly used in pulsar-timing-array (PTA) studies, and a continuous burst superposition, employed in ground-based GWB searches. In this work, we formally unify the two formalisms, showing that they provide discrete and continuous representations of the same underlying radiation process and converge on the scale-invariant spectrum plateau. On the rising low-frequency branch, where the first few harmonics dominate, the discrete nature becomes important, causing the two formalisms to diverge. Within this unified framework, the spectral calculation is more consistent across frequency bands, enabling multi-band inference. Leveraging this physical insight, we perform joint Bayesian inference across four representative loop-distribution models using the NANOGrav, EPTA, and LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA (LVK) datasets. By jointly sampling the string tension $Gμ$ alongside the average cusp and kink numbers $\{N_c, N_k\}$, the loop-radiation uncertainties are accounted for. We find that employing the harmonic expansion strengthens the LVK bounds by $21\%-31\%$ for three of these models. Additionally, the stringent LVK bounds preclude three of these models from explaining the observed PTA common signal. For the sole surviving model, our multi-band analysis improves the inferred limit on $Gμ$.

entry.title: Gauge-invariant nonperturbative Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics
entry.summary: By employing the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG), we study the renormalization group (RG) flow of a manifestly gauge- or Becchi--Rouet--Stora--Tyutin (BRST)-invariant nonperturbative ansatz of the one-particle irreducible (1PI) Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics. The gauge invariance of the Wilson action is \emph{exactly\/} preserved under the RG flow. We explicitly solve the GFERG equation in the leading and partially next-to-leading orders of the large-$N_f$ approximation, where $N_f$ is the number of flavors. We obtain gauge-invariant critical exponents and the gauge-invariant 1PI Wilson action at an infrared (IR) fixed point for~$D<4$, where $D$ is the spacetime dimension.

entry.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
entry.summary: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moiré effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.

entry.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
entry.summary: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor depending on the evaporation rate. Next, we discuss the changes that must be considered for the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. We find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation. The entangled global vacuum state again has a thermofield double structure with the modification mentioned above.

entry.title: The onset of the strong backreaction regime in axion inflation, an analytical study
entry.summary: Models where an axion-like inflaton is coupled to a $U(1)$ gauge field are theoretically well motivated and can display a rich phenomenology. The regime in which the quanta of the gauge field strongly backreact on the rolling inflaton has been studied for well more than a decade, and yet we cannot say that it is fully understood. In this paper we present an analytical study of the onset of the strong backreaction regime. Our formalism relies on a Laplace transform to convert a complicated integro-differential equation into the search of the poles of an analytic function. We confirm the existence, previously observed using a completely different formalism, of a stable region of strong backreaction. Our work provides, for the first time, analytical formulae that allow to study the evolution of the system as it transitions from the weak to the strong backreaction regime.

entry.title: From photometric surveys to HI intensity mapping: Improving constraints on magnification biases while testing gravity
entry.summary: The observed large-scale structure of the Universe is not a direct measure of the underlying distribution of matter. These observations are subtly distorted by gravitational lensing effects, which leave imprints on the statistical distribution of galaxies and offer a powerful test of general relativity. In this work, we investigate whether HI intensity mapping from current and forthcoming surveys can improve constraints on magnification lensing obtained from photometric galaxy surveys. In particular, we investigate whether one can jointly constrain the magnification bias parameters $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ and the amplitude of the Weyl potential, which we parametrise as $β$. We employ a Fisher matrix formalism in order to estimate future constraints on the magnification biases and $β$. We forecast constraints for three photometric surveys (DES-like, LSST-like, Euclid-like) individually and together with two HI intensity mapping surveys (MeerKLASS, SKAO). We apply the multi-tracer technique by combining each galaxy survey with each HI survey, exploiting the combined constraining in the overlapping sky area. The multi-tracer approach dramatically improves constraints on $β$ by factors of 18 to 50, depending on the surveys considered. For $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$, improvements can be marginal or by factors of 2 to 4. We also verify that $β$ and $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ can be constrained simultaneously as the cross-correlations between tracers break the degeneracies among them. We conclude that the multi-tracer combination of photometric galaxy surveys and HI intensity mapping surveys enables high-precision measurements of both $s^\mathrm{G}(z)$ and $β$. This opens an additional pathway to constrain $Φ+Ψ$ and test the validity of general relativity on cosmological scales.

entry.title: Supermassive Black Hole Winds in X-rays -- SUBWAYS. VI. Interplay between the soft X-ray excess and ultra-fast outflows
entry.summary: We present a broadband, multiwavelength study of the interplay between the soft X-ray excess (SE), ultra-fast outflows (UFOs), and warm absorbers (WAs) in 21 active galactic nuclei (AGN; 0.1 <= z <= 0.4) from the SUBWAYS project. We combine simultaneous or quasi-simultaneous UV, optical, and X-ray data from XMM-Newton (EPIC pn and OM), NuSTAR, and the Hubble Space Telescope. We model the SE using a two-coronae framework, in which a warm, optically thick corona (WC) produces the optical/UV and soft X-ray emission, while a hot, optically thin corona produces the hard X-ray continuum. We also test a hybrid model that adds relativistic reflection. The optical/UV coverage constrains the Comptonization seed photon temperature to 0.1-5.5 eV. The two-coronae model consistently describes the broadband emission, with WC electron temperatures kT_e ~ 0.1-0.9 keV and photon indices $Γ> 2$, consistent with previous studies. However, 9/21 AGN require the hybrid model, suggesting that the SE has multiple origins whose relative contributions vary. This is especially evident in UFO hosts, where 4/7 observations favor the hybrid model. Compared with sources without UFOs, UFO hosts show lower WC temperatures, harder hot-corona spectra, and positive hardness ratios. These trends should be treated cautiously because of the small sample and their dependence on spectral parameters and instrumental response. We find no significant differences between AGN with and without WAs. Our correlation analysis finds links between the amplification factor and WC temperature, WC optical depth and hardness ratio, and WC slope and optical depth with UV luminosity. We also find a tentative anticorrelation between WC optical depth and UFO outflow velocity.

entry.title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
entry.summary: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2π|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2π|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes as probes of black hole reentrant phase transitions
entry.summary: We investigate the interplay between thermodynamic phase transitions and the dynamical behavior of quasi-normal modes (QNMs) in weakly nonlinear charged anti-de Sitter black holes. In a non-extended phase space, we identify a reentrant large-small-large(intermediate) phase transition for these black holes. Employing the shooting method to solve the Klein-Gordon equation for a massless scalar field, we compute QNM frequencies across these phases, revealing distinct behaviors in different phases. Specifically, to our knowledge, this is the first report of utilizing QNMs as dynamical probes of thermodynamic phases during reentrant phase transitions including zeroth and first-order transitions. These findings establish QNMs as a powerful dynamical probe for thermodynamic phase transitions, providing new insights into the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of nonlinear charged black holes as well.

entry.title: Where should we look for the deviation from quantum mechanics?
entry.summary: We argue that the experimental measurement of the lifetime and decay law of metastable helium is a promising way to find a deviation from quantum mechanics. We analyze the decay of the metastable state for a quartic deformation of quantum mechanics. We find that the absolute change of the mean lifetime can be significant even if the modification is small. We show that, in the Wigner--Weisskopf approximation, the deviation from the exponential law in the modified theory can occur on time scales comparable with the lifetime.

entry.title: Tidal Disruption Events in Active Galactic Nuclei: Thermal Radiation and Jets
entry.summary: Over the past decade, dozens of Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) have been identified, with many more expected from upcoming surveys. A small subset has been observed to launch transient, highly luminous relativistic jets, for which the origin of the requisite magnetic flux has not been identified. A non-negligible fraction of TDEs are expected in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), where a magnetized accretion flow is already present. As shown first by Chan et al. (2019), the collision of a TDE debris stream with this flow can substantially alter both disk and debris dynamics, leading to a possibly Eddington-limited flare. Here, we use the Athena++ radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code to simulate the time near peak fallback rate of a TDE in an AGN, studying the debris-disk interaction, the radiation emitted, and the accumulation of magnetic flux near the horizon. In the example simulated, the accretion rate climbs to $\sim 12\,\dot{M}_{ \rm Edd}$, while the escaping solid angle-integrated luminosity approaches $\sim L_{ \rm Edd}$. The photon luminosity is strongly asymmetric, brighter in the hemisphere from which the debris strikes the disk and dimmer in the hemisphere toward which the debris travels. The photon spectrum peaks in the EUV. The polar magnetic flux grows $\sim 33$-fold, enough to raise the Blandford--Znajek luminosity by a factor $\sim 10^3$, reaching a level sufficient to power observed TDE jets. The polar magnetic flux is also asymmetric, likely making any jet similarly asymmetric, but in the opposite sense to the photon flux.

entry.title: The Structure in the Structure Function of Black Hole Light Curves
entry.summary: Of the two black holes, M87$^\ast$ and Sgr~A$^\ast$, for which event-horizon-scale imaging is currently achievable, only Sgr~A$^\ast$ at our Galactic Center exhibits sub-hour variability, making light curve observations of the inner accretion flow especially valuable for time-domain studies of the spacetime and the surrounding plasma. Observed light curves are often sampled with variable cadence, so a structure function is often used to quantify their variability properties. In this work, we assemble a heterogeneous Sgr~A$^\ast$ light curve data set from discrete observations acquired over $\sim12$ years at 230 GHz, with different instruments, durations, and cadences, and study its structure function in three frameworks. First, we consider analytic predictions for the features of structure functions of stationary random processes with Fourier spectra dictated by the Matérn covariance. We then study the structure functions resulting from lensed movies of synthetic optically thin accretion flows approximated with Matérn covariance in both space and time, and identify which features in the structure function can be attributed to the black-hole geometry. Lastly, we examine the structure functions of a library of $72$ general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations. We find that, in general, magnetically arrested disk (MAD) models produce smoother structure functions with steeper slopes than standard and normal evolution (SANE) counterparts. On time scales of $5-15$ minutes, the observed structure function slope of Sgr~A$^\ast$ more closely aligns with the MAD trend, while both simulation types are generally more variable than the data on all sub-hour timescales.

entry.title: Impact of Residual Gain Errors on the Detectability of Ionized Bubbles during Reionization with SKA 21-cm observations
entry.summary: Detecting ionized bubbles and characterizing their properties and the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM) using the HI 21-cm signal provides direct probes of cosmic reionization. Here, we focus on the detection of individual ionized bubbles around luminous sources using a matched-filter technique. We investigate the impact of time- and frequency-correlated residual antenna gain errors on the detectability and characterization of individual ionized regions with SKA-Low. We simulate mock SKA-Low AA* observations that include the HI 21-cm signal, astrophysical foregrounds, residual gain errors, and system noise corresponding to 100 h of observing time. We subtract the foreground components from the gain-corrupted data and subsequently apply the matched-filter technique to the residual visibilities. We find that the matched-filter technique is able to detect the ionized bubble and constrain its properties in the presence of residual gain errors with the rms amplitudes up to $σ_A\sim1\%$ and rms phases up to $σ_φ\sim1^\circ$. Residual gain errors at similar levels prevent the reliable identification of ionized regions in reconstructed HI 21-cm images and bias the estimated HI 21-cm power spectrum. Furthermore, we find that increasing the temporal correlation length increases the level of gain-induced artifacts in the reconstructed image. In contrast, increasing the frequency correlation length reduces these artifacts, as some fraction of the spectrally smooth gain-induced residuals is removed during foreground subtraction. We further find that the inferred bubble and IGM parameters remain largely unaffected by residual gain errors, although their uncertainties can increase. These results demonstrate the potential and robustness of the matched-filter technique for detecting and characterizing individual ionized bubbles in the presence of substantial residual calibration errors.

entry.title: Strain-Tunable High-$T_c$ Superconductivity in Layered R3m B$_2$CN
entry.summary: Using DFPT and Wannier-interpolated matrix elements in EPW, we find that isotropic tensile strain of 0--6\% narrows the B:2$p$/C:2$p$ bands at the Fermi level while softening the phonon branches most strongly coupled to them, driving the coupling constant $λ$ from 0.967 to 2.620. All four strained configurations remain mechanically and dynamically stable, satisfying the Born--Huang criteria with no imaginary phonon modes at any strain level. The fully anisotropic Migdal--Eliashberg equations give a $T_c$ that rises monotonically from 53.5~K to 84.5~K across the strain series, crossing the liquid-nitrogen boiling point at 6\% strain. The SISSO-based machine-learning model in EPW agrees with the anisotropic Migdal--Eliashberg $T_c$ values to within 10~K across the strain series.

entry.title: Probability measures for de Sitter JT gravity
entry.summary: Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity with positive cosmological constant is a toy model to study the emergence of expanding de Sitter universes from a quantum state. Its density matrix is a superposition of double-trumpet amplitudes which are solutions of a Wheeler-DeWitt equation. We compare predictions of such mixed states for classical expanding universes with the corresponding predictions of no-boundary wavefunctions. Double-trumpet amplitudes consistent with holography, whose semiclassical limit matches the result from Schwarzian boundary fluctuations, lead to a flat probability distribution for the size of the universe, consistent with models of inflation. This is in contrast to the suppression of large universes predicted by no-boundary wave functions.

entry.title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
entry.summary: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.

entry.title: A 4200-hour HyperFlash and ÉCLAT campaign on the hyperactive FRB 20240114A: constraining energetics with the most brilliant bursts
entry.summary: Hyperactive repeaters provide a unique window into the evolving environments and energy budgets of fast radio burst (FRB) sources, though they may not be representative of the FRB population in general. High-cadence observations are key to capturing the rarest and most energetic bursts, which occur only once per hundreds to thousands of hours. Here we present an unprecedented $4{,}200$-hour observing campaign targeting FRB 20240114A as part of the HyperFlash and ÉCLAT FRB monitoring programs. Over $806$ days, we detected $178$ high-energy ($\sim$$10^{40-42}$ erg) bursts with HyperFlash, which together amount to $4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg of released radio energy (assuming isotropic emission and 1-GHz emission bandwidth). The cumulative energy of the HyperFlash bursts is about twice that of $\sim$$11{,}000$ lower-energy bursts detected with FAST, emphasising the significant role that the highest-energy bursts play in depleting the central engine's stored energy. In fact, the single most brilliant burst from our sample, which we term the STROOP, contributes roughly $1/3$ of all the energy we measure, and is at the maximum energy seen in studies of both repeating and apparently one-off FRBs alike. We also find a break in the burst energy distribution at $\sim$$2\times10^{40}$ erg and a linear dispersion measure (DM) increase of $+0.96 \pm 0.06$ pc cm$^{-3}$ over a period of $318$ days. We discuss these findings in the context of a magnetar source model and highlight comparisons with the energetics of intermediate and giant X-ray/$γ$-ray flares from Galactic sources.

entry.title: Spectral Localization in Cavity-Mediated Entanglement Harvesting
entry.summary: We investigate the relation between spectral localization and entanglement harvesting in an analytically solvable model of two qubits coupled to a leaky single-mode cavity, which in turn couples to a continuous electromagnetic bath. We derive the no-jump concurrence at a prescribed reference gate time in closed form, $\mathcal C_g(Q)=2e^{-π/(2Q)}(1+e^{-π/(2Q)})/(1+3e^{-π/Q})$, where $Q\equiv|Δ|/κ$ is the ratio of the qubit-cavity detuning $Δ$ to the cavity linewidth $κ$. This reference time is inherited from the first maximally entangling unitary gate. At finite loss, $\mathcal C_g$ is the conditional concurrence at this prescribed readout time. In the high-$Q$ limit, $\mathcal C_g\simeq1-π^2/(16Q^2)$, while in the low-$Q$ limit it decays exponentially. For the Lorentzian spectral family, $Q$ is proportional to a detuning-normalized inverse participation ratio and simultaneously measures the balance between coherent exchange and collective decay. This yields a compact, model-specific description of the crossover from nearly unit conditional entanglement to overdamped suppression. The predicted $\mathcal C_g(Q)$ curve can, in principle, be examined in circuit QED with ideal monitoring and no-jump post-selection.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Fermionic Veneziano Amplitudes from Regge Zeros
entry.summary: We extend the Regge-zero bootstrap of the Veneziano amplitude to tree-level scattering with external fermions. We consider the colour-ordered four-point amplitude of a massless scalar and a massless spin-$\frac12$ fermion, in which fermionic resonances appear in the $s$-channel and bosonic resonances in the $t$-channel. Factoring out a spinor structure that carries the little-group weight of the amplitude, we bootstrap the resulting reduced amplitude, whose residues in each channel vanish at Regge zeros controlled by the trajectory of the opposite channel. Assuming ultrasoft Regge behaviour and that the residues have no zeros other than Regge zeros, we show that both Regge trajectories are linear and that the maximal spins grow with the level as $J_F=n+\frac12$ and $J_B=m+1$. Duality between the fermionic- and bosonic-pole expansions then fixes the reduced amplitude to a Beta function, up to its normalisation and the ratio of the two Regge slopes. Requiring the fermionic and bosonic spectra to be degenerate equates the slopes, and the resulting amplitude coincides with the open superstring amplitude.

entry.title: Characterizing Fermionic Non-Gaussianity in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model via Replica Twist Entropy
entry.summary: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems plays a central role in modern many-body physics. Intriguing insights emerge from investigating how quantum resources, which are essential for achieving unambiguous quantumness, are generated and spread under chaotic quantum dynamics. In fermionic systems, non-Gaussianity constitutes an important resource beyond entanglement, characterizing the deviation of generic quantum states from free-fermion states. In this Letter, we propose using the \textit{replica twist entropy}, defined through the expectation value of a replica rotation operator with a tunable angle $α$, as a natural probe of non-Gaussianity in pure fermionic states. After deriving its behavior for typical many-body states, we establish a general framework for analyzing the replica twist entropy in solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models in the large-$N$ limit. Applying this framework to the dynamics of the thermofield double state, we uncover a novel dynamical phase diagram in the parameter space of $α$ and evolution time $t$, exhibiting spontaneous $Z_2$ symmetry breaking at $α=π/4$ and universal cusps as a function of $α$ in the long-time regime. Our results pave the way for studying non-Gaussianity in strongly correlated fermionic systems and reveal a new class of dynamical transitions probed by non-Gaussianity.

entry.title: Gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
entry.summary: We perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. We show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early Universe affect the GW spectrum. We derive simple analytical expressions for the GW spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and laser interferometers. We analyze the latest data from PTAs and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nHz data from NANOGrav, but are excluded by 3.2 nHz data at $3σ$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. We also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by NANOGrav-15 data at $3σ$, they are completely compatible with EPTA and PPTA data. Finally, we study correlations between GW signals at PTAs and laser interferometers.

entry.title: Global isometric embedding of the Kerr spacetime and beyond
entry.summary: We construct a new isometric embedding of the Kerr spacetime into $(5+7)$-dimensional flat spacetime. It is asymptotically flat, covers the entire $r>0$ region and has a very simple form. We also show how this embedding can be generalized to any spacetime admitting a Kerr-Schild-like decomposition of the metric.

entry.title: Microwave probing of magnetic phases in a dipolar-exchange magnet LiGdF$_4$
entry.summary: We report the results of low-temperature magnetic resonance measurements performed on a single-crystal sample of a weakly anisotropic dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet LiGdF$_4$. The transformation of a resonance spectrum due to the formation of the ordered phase is observed at temperatures below $T_N=0.19(1)$ K. A sequence of field-induced phase transitions is detected for the external magnetic field applied along the fourfold axis of the crystal. A well-resolved magnetic resonance spectrum is observed in one of the low-field magnetic phases as well as above the saturation field. Competing exchange and dipolar interactions, as a special type of magnetic frustration, are suggested to account for the delayed ordering and complex magnetic phase diagram of the system.

entry.title: Weak Cosmic Censorship in Einstein-Born-Infeld Black Hole: A Parameter-Space Analysis
entry.summary: Einstein-Born-Infeld is a charged black hole solution of general relativity with Born-Infeld nonlinear electrodynamics, which has interesting physical features. It violates Bekenstein's entropy upper bound, and it can overcharge with respect to the Reissner-Nordström black hole. It presents an optimum situation to test the cosmic censorship conjecture, which is another important conjecture in black hole physics. In principle, this analysis requires the calculation of the self-energy of a test particle in the vicinity of the black hole, which, in general, is not feasible because of the electromagnetic nonlinearities. In this work, we propose an alternative approach that allows us to explore the whole parameter space of the Einstein-Born-Infeld black hole and test the validity of the cosmic censorship conjecture.

entry.title: First-Principles Effective Mass in the Three-Dimensional Uniform Electron Gas
entry.summary: The quasiparticle effective mass $m^*$ of the three-dimensional uniform electron gas (UEG) is a fundamental Fermi-liquid parameter whose value and density dependence have remained controversial for decades. Using renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms, we determine $m^*$ in the metallic regime ($r_s \le 6$) from first principles by two complementary routes -- the self-energy and the forward-scattering four-point vertex via the $p$-wave spin-symmetric Landau parameter $F_1^s$ -- that agree within uncertainties at each density through sixth renormalized order. The resulting $m^*/m$ remains close to unity throughout the metallic regime, with a shallow non-monotonic density dependence -- a minimum near $r_s\approx 1$ followed by a gentle upturn -- reflecting the interplay of exchange and dynamical screening in the self-energy, and disfavoring strong monotonic suppression. This finding supports a physical picture for the metallic UEG in which dominant charge correlations are concentrated in nearly forward scattering and generate only a weak $F_1^s$ component.

entry.title: Morphological Bias: How Ellipticals and Spirals Trace the Cosmic Web Differently
entry.summary: We present a data-driven measurement of galaxy bias and scale-dependent relative bias for elliptical and spiral galaxies using angular auto- and cross-power spectra from DES and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR8. We introduce the cross-tracer clustering ratio (CTCR), the ratio of auto- to cross-power spectra, which isolates the relative clustering of morphological tracers as a function of angular multipole $\ell$. Across both surveys, ellipticals are more strongly clustered than spirals; the cleanest constraints come from DESI, where the two redshift distributions are well matched. The difference is scale dependent: the relative bias is near unity on large scales ($\ell \lesssim 50$) and rises toward smaller scales, reaching $2.9$--$4.0σ$ per bin at $\ell = 200$ with an inverse-variance-weighted amplitude $Δb = +0.56 \pm 0.06$. A complementary linear-bias analysis confirms that ellipticals are positively biased relative to the matter field, while spirals are consistent with weak bias or anti-bias. The results are robust to two covariance estimators, contamination tests, luminosity splits, and comparisons with two N-body mock catalogs. Throughout, we present the CTCR as an \emph{effective} clustering ratio that is an upper bound on the physical bias ratio, adopting an assumption-light strategy appropriate for a first measurement; the joint multi-spectrum decomposition required to extract the physical bias ratio is identified as future work. These findings provide empirical evidence that galaxy morphology imprints both the amplitude and scale dependence of galaxy bias, and establish the CTCR as a useful observable for testing halo occupation and assembly-bias models with future imaging surveys.

entry.title: Closing the Loop: from EPRL-FK spinfoams to Regge dynamics
entry.summary: We study the semiclassical limit of the EPRL-FK model on a fixed simplicial complex. We ask what additional condition is needed for its variational principle to reproduce the equations of motion of Regge calculus, the standard discretization of General Relativity. This limit differs and complements the definition of the semiclassical regime in which, for suitable boundary states and a sufficiently refined simplicial complex, spinfoam amplitudes approximate gravitational transition amplitudes to a prescribed accuracy. We recast the EPRL-FK model in wedge-holonomy variables and identify geometric closure as the missing condition. We prove that imposing geometric closure as an additional constraint alongside local flatness allows us to reconstruct curved geometries. On a regular, nondegenerate Lorentzian branch with spacelike tetrahedra, these constraints define a surface equivalent to the space of length-Regge geometries, modulo gauge. The wedge action restricted to this surface becomes the Regge action, and variations tangent to this surface yield the length-Regge equations. We propose a way to implement geometric closure directly in the spinfoam amplitude. With this additional constraint, the EPRL-FK model is equivalent to Regge calculus in its semiclassical regime on a fixed simplicial complex.

entry.title: Reconstructing BPS String Charge Cone in 6d N=(1,0) Supergravity
entry.summary: The tensor branch of six-dimensional $\mathcal N=(1,0)$ supergravity is characterized by a spectrum of BPS strings charged under the two-form gauge fields. Their charges span a cone in the tensor charge lattice, whose extremal rays are generated by primitive BPS string charges that become tensionless at the boundaries of the tensor moduli space. We develop a systematic procedure, based entirely on effective field theory data, to reconstruct the primitive BPS string generators and thereby determine the complete closed BPS string cone of any 6d $(1,0)$ supergravity theory. The key ingredients are the universal {\it H}-string, which allows us to isolate a fixed sector determined by classified LST blocks and gauge anomaly data from the remaining gauge-neutral E-string sector, and a BPS refinement of the Completeness Conjecture that ensures population of the relevant charge rays. We further show that this reconstruction provides new constraints on the low-energy theory and can rule out candidate EFTs that pass all previously known local lattice and anomaly consistency conditions. Separately, for theories admitting geometric tensor bases, we explain how the same reconstruction determines the complete Mori cone of the corresponding Kähler surface.

entry.title: Interaction and disorder effects on Cooper instability in two-dimensional fractional Dirac semimetals
entry.summary: Employing a renormalization group analysis that allows for an unbiased treatment of competing physical ingredients, we systematically trace how the interplay between Cooper pairing and disorder scatterings governs the emergence or suppression of Cooper instability in the low-energy regime of fractional Dirac semimetals.In the clean limit, we find that the emergence of Cooper instability requires surpassing a finite interaction threshold $|λ_c|$, and depends sensitively on both the fractional exponent $α$ and the transfer momentum $\mathbf{Q}=(Q,φ)$. Specifically, bigger values of $α$ enhance the tendency toward BCS instability. For $α\in(0.001,0.61)$, the $(Q,φ)$ parameter space separates into two distinct regions: Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral1}, where Cooper instability is suppressed, and Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral2}, where it is allowed. In the presence of disorders, we demonstrate that they can either promote or suppress Cooper instability. Disorder of type $Δ_1$ or $Δ_2$ enhances superconductivity by reducing the critical interaction threshold $|λ_c|$ and expanding the superconducting phase space (Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral2}). In sharp contrast, either $Δ_0$ or $Δ_3$ suppresses Cooper pairing by increasing $|λ_c|$ and shrinking the available phase space (Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral1}). Although Cooper instability can be enhanced when promotive disorders ($Δ_1$, $Δ_2$) coexist with a single suppressive disorder ($Δ_0$ or $Δ_3$), the suppressive influence of $Δ_{0,3}$ generally dominates the promotive effects of $Δ_{1,2}$ in the presence of all sorts of disorders. These results would be helpful for further studies of fractional Dirac semimetals and alike materials.

entry.title: Spin-Inversion Degeneracies in Restricted Inspiral Waveforms for LISA
entry.summary: Spin inversions appear in several settings. Analytical work predicts a single spin flip during unequal-mass supermassive binary inspiral, while numerical relativity and post-Newtonian calculations show repeated flip-flop motion in comparable-mass binaries. Secular spin evolution also predicts additional cases driven by spin-induced mass quadrupoles. Whether these effects can be distinguished in gravitational-wave data is still unclear. We combine the secular spin angle equations with a quasi-circular second post-Newtonian frequency evolution and build a restricted waveform weighted by the sky-averaged LISA sensitivity. We study five near-equal-mass injections with detector-frame total mass $M=2\times10^5M_\odot$, including Kerr flip-flops and one quadrupole-induced case. Each injection is compared with physically evolving waveforms constrained to have no orbital-plane crossings. We search all four no-inversion sectors, vary the masses, spin magnitudes, and initial spin angles, and maximize over time, phase, and overall amplitude. Large spin motion does not by itself lead to a clearly different waveform in this restricted model. We compare configurations with different spin magnitudes, relative spin orientations, and angular excursions at eleven observer inclinations between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. With each injection normalized to signal SNR $ρ_\star=100$, four of the five cases leave a residual SNR below unity for the $0^\circ$ viewing direction along the total angular momentum. At nonzero inclinations, the residual associated with the largest match found reaches $7.07$ in the two-active-spin case at $55^\circ$. These upper bounds on the minimum residual within the allowed template family suggest potential distinguishability of spin inversions and motivate studies with more complete waveforms and the full LISA response.

entry.title: Holomorphic extremal surfaces for pseudoentropy in dS/CFT
entry.summary: We formulate the extremization problem for codimension-two hypersurfaces in de Sitter space in holomorphic coordinates, with real anchoring conditions at future infinity. The resulting equation ($K^I=0$) describes complex bulk realizations extending the usual piecewise Hartle--Hawking construction. We compute holographic pseudoentropy for harmonic deformations of spherical regions of arbitrary size and dimension, confirming its universal expansion through second order in the deformation parameter. The result is independent of the integration contour within each homology class on the complexified extremal surface. Inequivalent classes, labeled by an integer associated with a discrete global-coordinate isometry, differ by a sign of the universal term in odd boundary dimensions and by real finite shifts in even dimensions. For conical defects in dS$_3$ parametrized by a Schwarzschild-dS mass, we also verify the first law of pseudoentropy and the persistence of contour degeneracy within each homology class.

entry.title: Complexification of the Kerr-AdS black hole thermodynamic phase transition
entry.summary: In this paper, we establish a systematic complex-analytical framework for investigating the thermodynamics of high-dimensional singly spinning Kerr-AdS black holes. By performing an analytical continuation of the black hole horizon radius into the complex plane, we map the thermodynamic behavior for the black hole to the zeros distribution of the corresponding analytical function. In the region below the critical point, this approach provides the criterion for identifying phase transitions and reveals that the zeroth-order phase transition does not alter the underlying thermodynamic topological structure of the black hole. In the supercritical region, based on the Lee-Yang theory of phase transition, we construct the Widom line to characterize the supercritical crossover behavior for the Kerr-AdS black holes. This study provides a new perspective on the thermodynamic analysis of black holes.

entry.title: Gate-Switchable Josephson Diode Effect in Graphene via Magnetochiral Anisotropy
entry.summary: The Josephson diode effect originating from magnetochiral anisotropy has thus far been realized primarily in conventional two-dimensional electron gases. Here, we propose a graphene-based Josephson junction as a broadly gate-tunable platform for nonreciprocal supercurrent transport. We demonstrate that the nonreciprocal critical current not only reverses its sign when graphene is switched from $n$- to $p$-type doping via electrostatic gating, but its efficiency can also be continuously tuned from zero up to $\sim 40\%$. This gate-controlled polarity switching and efficiency modulation---unique to the chiral nature of Dirac fermions in graphene---has no counterpart in conventional semiconductor systems, positioning the graphene Josephson diode as a highly versatile component for advanced superconducting circuits.

entry.title: Effects of Viscosity on Sloshing Cold Fronts in Galaxy Clusters
entry.summary: The viscous properties of the intracluster medium (ICM) remain poorly constrained. Cold fronts-sharp discontinuities formed during cluster mergers-offer a potential avenue to probe the effective viscosity of the ICM. Velocity shear across these fronts should generate Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities (KHI), unless viscosity or magnetic tension suppresses them. We perform cluster merger simulations incorporating four ICM viscosity models: (A) inviscid, (B) isotropic Spitzer viscosity, (C) anisotropic Braginskii viscosity, and (D) Braginskii viscosity limited by microinstabilities. The isotropic Spitzer viscosity (case B) strongly suppresses KHI, producing smooth cold front surfaces, while the inviscid (A) and microinstability-limited (D) cases show prominent ripples. The Braginskii case (C) yields intermediate suppression. We also vary the plasma $β$ parameter ($β\approx$ 100 and 1600) to examine how a changing magnetic field strength affects the results. Stronger magnetic fields further suppress KHI, leading to smoother fronts and reduced differences between different viscosity models, while also widening the range of permitted pressure anisotropies when microinstability-based limiters are present. These results indicate that both viscosity and magnetic fields play crucial roles in stabilising sloshing cold fronts in galaxy clusters.

entry.title: Radius of the innermost stable circular orbit of black-holes with localized Astrophysical Dark Matter halo
entry.summary: We investigate the geodesic structure of a static, spherically symmetric black-hole in the background of a localized Astrophysical Dark Matter (ADM)-halo. The halo is modeled by a core-radius ($r_0$), regularized density profile that vanishes at the event horizon and exponential factor ensures the finite total halo mass. We solved the Einstein field equations numerically with equation of state with $p=wρ$ for stiff matter $w=1$ scenario. By analyzing the effective potential and its first and second derivatives, we evaluated the characteristic radius of the time-like innermost stable circular orbit ($r_{\text{ISCO}}$) of massive particle in the vicinity of hairy black-hole. Our numerical analysis is consistent with the recently proposed theoretical upper bound $r_{\text{ISCO}} \le 6$ normalized to unit mass black-hole. We showed that the ADM-halo shifts $r_{\text{ISCO}}$ inward with respect to the Schwarzschild (bald) scenario and the shifts are larger for larger halo core-radius. In particular our numerical finding enumerate $r_{\text{ISCO}}$ are approximately $5.97$, $5.61$, $5.53$ for $r_0=2.0,10.0,20.0$ respectively. We believe that our analysis with ADM-halo model shed light on probing black-hole hair through high-energy astrophysical observables.

entry.title: Static spherically symmetric Kundt vacuum solutions of higher-derivative gravities
entry.summary: We study static spherically symmetric Kundt solutions to the vacuum field equations of quadratic gravity with a cosmological constant, as well as specific models of six-derivative gravity. In quadratic gravity, we identify all solutions for coupling constants satisfying ${α\neq3β}$, while the case ${α=3β}$ is studied using the Frobenius method, where we derive the recurrence relations for the power series. In contrast, in six-derivative gravity, we focus on selected models to illustrate the variety of closed-form solutions; we also analyze possible indicial families of Frobenius solutions. For all solutions, we analyze curvature singularities and their accessibility to geodesic observers. We then construct exact gravitational-wave solutions propagating on some of these backgrounds in quadratic and six-derivative gravity. It is known that in Einstein gravity, gravitational waves on the Nariai background unavoidably contain singularities, which are interpreted as physical sources generating these gravitational waves. In contrast, in addition to singular solutions, for appropriate values of the coupling constants, higher-order gravities allow for globally smooth solutions representing gravitational waves.

entry.title: Clumpy Outflows from Super-Eddington Accreting Black Holes. II. Conditions for Clump Formation
entry.summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) commonly exhibit ultra-fast outflows (UFOs) with velocities of $0.03$--$0.3~c$. Recent high-resolution X-ray observations with XRISM/Resolve suggest that UFOs may have a clumpy structure. However, the formation and evolution of these clumpy outflows remain poorly understood. In the first paper of this series, we investigated the formation of clumpy outflows using numerical simulations and find that sufficiently high spatial resolution is required to reproduce clumpy structures numerically. In this second paper, we perform a series of numerical experiments to identify the key physical processes governing clump formation. We find that spatial fluctuations of physical quantities at the disk surface are essential for the formation of clumpy outflows, whereas spatial and temporal fluctuations at the inner boundary have only a minor effect. Furthermore, density structure-function analysis suggests that the high-density regions have an elongated morphology with characteristic transverse widths of several tens of $R_{\rm g}$, possibly produced by radiation Rayleigh--Taylor instability. A more comprehensive investigation of the instability in general-relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, where accretion disk structures emerge self-consistently, is expected to provide deeper insights into the physical origin of clumpy outflows.

entry.title: Electrostatic lens of a charged vortex
entry.summary: We study the local electrostatic response of a charged superfluid in the presence of a cylindrically symmetric vortex, allowing both the particle density and the thermodynamic compressibility to vary with the radial coordinate. Starting from the electrostatic charge response obtained from the phase-only Popov action, we introduce a local-density extension and derive the regular near-axis expansion of the scalar potential. The constant, quadratic, and quartic coefficients are obtained explicitly in terms of the local screening response and of the leading nonuniform contribution to the vortex density profile. For a three-dimensional unitary Fermi equation of state, the density dependence of the compressibility generates a definite thermodynamic contribution to the quartic coefficient. The resulting decomposition separates this equation-of-state contribution from the ordinary constant-screening and charge-source terms that occur at the same order. This provides a compact analytical connection between vortex-core thermodynamics and the local electrostatic profile of a charged superfluid.

entry.title: The relativistic reason for quantum probability amplitudes
entry.summary: We show that the quantum-mechanical probability distribution involving complex probability amplitudes can be derived from three natural conditions imposed on a relativistically invariant probability function describing the motion of a particle that can take multiple paths simultaneously. The conditions are: (i) pairwise Kolmogorov additivity, (ii) time symmetry, and (iii) Bayes' rule. The resulting solution, parameterized by a single constant, is the squared modulus of a sum of complex exponentials of the relativistic action, thereby recovering the Feynman path-integral formulation of quantum mechanics.

entry.title: Turning Number and the Geometry of Disorder-Induced Topology
entry.summary: The geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps derived from the zero-frequency single-particle Green's function provides a route to a refined topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit. The central idea is to complement standard topological invariants by invariants that characterize the geometry of the map itself. As a paradigmatic example, we study the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with disorder, where the topological Hamiltonian defines a planar Bloch loop. In addition to its conventional winding number, this loop possesses an integer turning number that characterizes the winding of its tangent vector. We identify turning-number transitions that occur while the topological Hamiltonian remains finite and spectrally gapped, driven solely by a vanishing tangent vector of the Bloch loop, and obtain an extended phase diagram with additional topological structure beyond the winding-number classification. Asymptotic analysis predicts the emergence and disorder dependence of the corresponding transition regime, in agreement with the numerical results. Our findings establish the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps as an additional source of topological structure beyond conventional classifications.

entry.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
entry.summary: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the recently synthesized van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.

entry.title: Static tidal Love numbers of Schwarzschild and non-Schwarzschild black holes in quadratic gravity
entry.summary: We calculate the static electric quadrupolar response of black holes in four-dimensional quadratic gravity, with action $R-αC^2+βR^2$. The Schwarzschild solution has zero massless gravitational Love number under the stated boundary conditions. A numerical non-Schwarzschild solution instead has a nonzero negative response. At $α/r_h^2=1/2$, we find $λ_E/r_h^5\simeq-0.1224928$ and $k_2^{(r_h)}\simeq-0.1837391$, with a final outer-endpoint change in $k_2^{(r_h)}$ of about $1.60\times10^{-7}$. We explain how the background is obtained by shooting and how the tidal solution is selected by matching at an intermediate radius. The perturbations are written in Kodama--Ishibashi gauge-invariant variables. After the scalar-curvature perturbation is excluded by horizon regularity and the absence of an applied scalar tide, the remaining static sector has three coupled second-order radial equations. We define the curvature amplitudes in these equations and describe why simple attempts to separate them fail. The coupling scan shows a negative response approaching zero near the Schwarzschild intersection. We also explain why this full-theory result does not conflict with the removal of curvature-squared operators in a perturbative low-energy expansion.

entry.title: Galactic warps constrain equivalence-principle violation in the dark sector
entry.summary: Current measurements of the expansion of the Universe allow for the presence of evolving dark energy, distinct from a cosmological constant, with an equation of state that seems to violate the null energy condition. One notable explanation for this behaviour is that the dark energy interacts with the dark matter, violating the equivalence principle yet evading conventional laboratory and astrophysical constraints. Such models produce fifth forces acting only on dark matter. We show how such forces separate halo and stellar disk centres, creating a potential gradient across the disk that warps it into a cup shape. Measuring the warps of $4\times10^3$ edge-on disks in Sloan Digital Sky Survey images and modelling the fifth-force signal together with competing baryonic effects, we find no sign of the predicted correlation between the measured warps and the fifth-force field. This constrains the fifth-force strength relative to gravity to $ΔG/G_N<7.7\times10^{-4}$ at 95% credibility (or $<1.7\times10^{-3}$ once systematic uncertainties are included) for force ranges of 8 Mpc and above. In the infinite-range limit of a scalar rolling today, even the conservative bound is three times stronger than the tightest cosmological bound (which, unlike ours, depends on the scalar's cosmological evolution) and about two orders of magnitude below other astrophysical bounds. It disfavours at 2-3$σ$ the couplings preferred by recent fits of interacting dark energy to cosmological data unless gravitational screening is invoked.

entry.title: Dualities and Topological Classification of the $S=1$ Pyrochlore Spin Ice
entry.summary: We derive dual descriptions of the trivial paramagnetic, $\mathbb{Z}_2$-deconfined, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-confined U(1) Coulomb phases of the $S=1$ pyrochlore spin ice. In the monopole-free limit, the system can be effectively mapped onto 3D $XY$ and Ising loop-gas models depending on the spin anisotropy, which provides theoretical estimates for the phase boundaries, while a macroscopic flux vector classifies the topological sectors via geometric parity rules. Thermal unit monopoles permit endpoints of both directed spin loops and unoriented vacancy loops. The resulting relevant symmetry-breaking fields in the dual $XY$ and Ising descriptions predict rounded crossovers near the monopole-free critical points. Monte Carlo simulations support this monopole-induced rounding.

entry.title: Quasi-bound states and late-time evolution of a massive fermion around a Reissner-Nordström black hole
entry.summary: A massive fermion around a charged black hole provides a gravitational analogue of atomic bound states and their relaxation. In this work, we study this system by formulating the radial equation as a coupled matrix system and constructing the Green's function with ingoing boundary conditions at the horizon and decaying boundary conditions at infinity. In the weak-coupling scenario $|qQ|\sim mM<1$, a matrix matching scheme gives an improved analytic expression of quasi-bound-state spectrum, including fine-structure corrections and more accurate decay widths. The extremal Reissner-Nordström case ($|Q|=M$) is treated separately and shown to be the smooth limiting result of the non-extremal spectrum. We further analyze the branch-cut contribution to the time-domain Green's function in the late-time limit. We confirm an oscillatory power-law behavior in intermediate late-time regime $1/m < t < 1/m^3M^2$. In the far late-time regime $t>1/m^3M^2$, the activation of the quasi-bound states produces an $t^{-5/6}\exp(-ηt^{1/3})$ suppression with a chirping phase before the asymptotic $t^{-5/6}$ tail previously found in the limit $t\to\infty$. Direct time-domain simulations support this distinction and show how the quasi-bound contribution coexists with the familiar power-law component.

entry.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
entry.summary: We develop a self-contained theoretical framework that classifies the topological phases and critical phenomena of classical pyrochlore magnets with arbitrary spin $S$, subject to competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies. We work first in the monopole-free (ice-rule) limit. In the small-$w$ regime, where the single-ion term favors low spin amplitudes, dualities reveal a dichotomy: Integer spins exhibit a continuous 3D $XY$ deconfinement transition, whereas half-integer spins remain in a $U(1)$ Coulomb liquid without any transition. In the large-$w$ regime, where $|S^z| = S$, the macroscopic flux is quantized to multiples of $2S$. Mapping the defect structure to loop gases, we prove that the ice rule is compatible with the modular $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ flux conservation at the vertex level if and only if $S \le 3/2$. For $S=3/2$, this maps the system to the three-state Potts model, whose symmetry-allowed cubic invariant drives a first-order transition. For $S \ge 2$, no discrete clock mapping exists; a decomposition of the partition function shows that the only processes sensitive to the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ structure carry exponentially small weight and correspond to irrelevant operators at the 3D $XY$ fixed point, so the deconfinement transition is of the 3D $XY$ type. Finally, incorporating thermal monopoles, we show that they act as a symmetry-breaking effective magnetic field that severs defect strings. Consequently, the continuous transitions are rounded into crossovers, whereas the first-order $S=3/2$ transition is predicted to survive at finite temperatures, terminating at a critical end point. Classical Monte Carlo simulations for $S$ up to $7/2$ corroborate the predicted crossovers at the accessible temperatures, which lie above the estimated critical end point, so the survival of the $S=3/2$ first-order transition remains to be tested directly.

entry.title: Strong generation of the chiral algebra of $\mathcal N=4$~$SU(N)$ super Yang--Mills theory
entry.summary: The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic--odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.

entry.title: Relaxation Dynamics of Superconducting/Normal Interfaces in the Intermediate State of a type-I superconductor
entry.summary: The dynamics of phase boundaries, such as superconducting/normal (S/N) interfaces in type-I superconductors, are typically obscured in conventional magnetic measurements, which are strongly influenced by surface barriers and global flux processes. Here, we employ the complex ac magnetostrictive coefficient as a sensitive probe of the bulk dynamics of S/N interfaces in the intermediate state of lead. The ac magnetostrictive coefficient exhibits an unusual complex response, with a negative real component and a positive imaginary component. Frequency-dependent measurements show that the magnitude of the real component decreases monotonically with increasing frequency, whereas the imaginary component first increases, reaches a broad maximum, and then decreases. In contrast, ac susceptibility displays a conventional Debye-type magnetic relaxation with a different phase relation between its real and imaginary components. We propose that the magnetostrictive response arises from ac-field-driven relaxation and rearrangement of metastable S/N domain configurations toward states of lower free energy. These results reveal a distinct interfacial relaxation channel in the intermediate state and establish the complex ac magnetostrictive coefficient as a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium S/N interface dynamics.

entry.title: Improving Slow-Roll Estimates in Starobinsky Inflation Using an Analytic Hubble Parameter
entry.summary: Inflationary observables are naturally formulated in terms of the Hubble-flow hierarchy. Because exact background solutions are often unavailable, the Hubble-flow parameters are commonly approximated using potential slow-roll (PSR) quantities constructed from derivatives of the inflationary potential. We revisit the accuracy of this replacement for Starobinsky inflation by mapping analytic Jordan-frame background variables to their Einstein-frame counterparts and deriving the Hubble-flow parameters directly. The leading analytic background is an exact solution of a controlled deformation of the Starobinsky action. Linearizing the pure Starobinsky equation about this background yields a closed-form perturbative correction. Using the same first-order spectral expressions throughout, the perturbatively corrected background tracks the numerical evolution of the first two Hubble-flow parameters more accurately than the next-to-leading-order (NLO) PSR approximation over the common domain in which the NLO expressions remain physical. Moreover, the NLO estimate of \(\widetildeε_1\) reaches a maximum value of approximately \(0.114\), subsequently decreases, and therefore cannot determine the end of inflation from \(\widetildeε_1=1\). For the Planck 2018 central value \(n_s=0.9649\), the perturbatively corrected background gives \(\widetilde{N}_*\simeq55.60\), compared with \(55.72\) for the converged numerical background and \(56.98\) for the conventional large-\(\widetilde{N}_*\) estimate. For the adopted ACT DR6 combined-data value \(n_s=0.974\), it gives \(\widetilde{N}_*\simeq75.43\), compared with the conventional value \(76.92\). The analytic construction therefore provides a self-consistent endpoint and a first-order estimate of the e-fold number that closely reproduces the converged numerical result.
